LanguageData.RimFeast_InviteGizmoDesc: Send a messenger with gifts to invite a noble house to a feast at this spot. Costs {0} silver for a house that has never dined with you. A house that has feasted here recently asks for richer gifts, and is harder to impress a second time. Let a season pass and the novelty returns.
LanguageData.RimFeast_InviteDisabledBusy: a feast is already planned or underway
LanguageData.RimFeast_InviteDisabledNoHouses: No noble house will treat with you.
LanguageData.RimFeast_NotEnoughSilver: Not enough silver around your home to pay the messenger ({0} needed).
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextInviteSent: A messenger rides out with gifts and your invitation to {0}. If all goes well, a cortege will arrive within a day or so.\n\nSet a fine table before they do: food and drink laid out around the feast spot, in a hall worth showing off.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextGuestsArrive: A cortege from {0} has arrived for the feast: {1} guests riding under their house banner. They are making for your feast hall.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageFeastBegins: The feast begins. The guests of {0} take their places.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextCortegeGift: The cortege of {0} did not come empty-handed. {1} sets a present down at the head of the table before sitting:\n\n{2}
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageBrawl: {0} and {1} have come to blows over their cups!
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageToast: A toast is raised to {0}. The hall falls quiet to listen.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextFeastTriumph: The banquet for {0} was the stuff of songs: a proud hall, a groaning table, drink flowing all night. The house rides home full of praise.\n\nAs thanks, their lord left a purse of {1} silver on your table.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextFeastGood: The guests of {0} ate and drank well. They leave in high spirits and will speak kindly of your hall.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextFeastDecent: The banquet for {0} was decent enough, though nobody will sing about it. The guests take their leave politely.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextFeastPoor: The banquet for {0} fell flat: thin fare, a dry table, or a hall not worth the name. The guests leave unimpressed, and word of it will travel.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextLeaderRides: {0}, head of house {1}, rides with the cortege in person. Hosting the head of a house is a rare honor, and a heavier charge.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextLeaderHonored: The head of the house sat at your table in person: the honor done to {0} is all the greater.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextLeaderShamed: The head of the house saw it all in person. A thin table served under those eyes costs more than a thin table.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextPoorTravels: A poor table travels as far as a rich one. House {0} thinks a little less of you.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextBetrayed: Blood has been drawn by your hand, under your own roof. The guests of {0} draw steel and fight their way toward the gates. What the house makes of it will depend on how many make it home.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextRedWedding: Of the cortege of {0}, {1} never left your hall alive and free. Word of a host who slaughters guests at table will reach every house on the rim: {0} swears vengeance and will come for blood, and no house will break bread under your roof for a long while.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextBloodSpilled: A guest of {0} came to harm by your hand, and the cortege fled your hall. The house will remember this breach of the guest right.
LanguageData.RimFeast_InviteRefusedBetrayed: will never break bread with you again
LanguageData.RimFeast_InviteRefusedWord: word of the red feast still travels
LanguageData.RimFeast_SpotFleeing: The guests of {0} are fleeing your hall.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SpotLeaving: The guests of {0} are taking their leave.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageTakingWounded: The guests of {0} gather their wounded to carry them home.
LanguageData.RimFeast_QualHallMid: The hall makes a fair showing.
LanguageData.RimFeast_QualDrinkMid: There is drink, but it is measured.
LanguageData.RimFeast_QualEntHigh: The hall rings with toasts and music.
LanguageData.RimFeast_PreviewHeader: As the table stands, for the {0} guests expected:
LanguageData.RimFeast_CancelInviteDesc: Recall the messenger before {0} sets out. The gifts are already spent, and they are not coming back.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageInviteCancelled: The messenger is recalled. {0} will not be coming.
LanguageData.RimFeast_WardAwayLine: {0} is being raised at the court of {1}, home in about {2}.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetGift: Gift after a legendary feast: {0} silver
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetCortege: Cortege size: about {0} guests (houses send {1} to {2} depending on how they see you)
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetSummon: Colonists drop their work for the feast
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetSummonTip: When the guests sit down, colonists set aside whatever they were doing and head for the hall. Surgery, tending and other jobs that cannot be dropped are left alone. Turn this off and they will drift in one by one as their work ends, the way vanilla parties fill up.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetLeader: Heads of house may attend in person
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetLeaderTip: With high goodwill and a feast already to your name, the head of the house may ride with the cortege. Hosting them is worth more, and losing them costs more.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetTradePactTip: A good feast sends one of the house merchants your way within a few days.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetMarriageTip: A noble may ask for the hand of one of your colonists. Accepting means losing them to the house for good.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetBrawlChance: Drunken brawl chance: {0}% per drunk guest, per check
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetTreachery: Guests in your hall may come with poison
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetTreacheryTip: Below the goodwill threshold, an invitation may be accepted with bad intentions. Turn this off and a cold house is merely cold.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetCensoredMusic: Use the alternate red feast tune
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetCensoredMusicTip: The red feast plays a cover of a certain song from a certain show. Tick this to use a different track instead, same scene, same cue, no copyright worries.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetFadeDays: A house forgets one feast every {0} days
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetRedWeddingDays: Word of a red feast travels for {0} days
LanguageData.RimFeast_TrapGizmoDesc: Send the same messenger and the same gifts, but this feast is a trap. Once the guests are at the table you can mark them for the knife, one by one. The house will never forgive it, word will travel to every hall, and your own people will carry the shame. The plate armor, though, stays.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageNoAssassin: Nobody is able to do the deed.
LanguageData.RimFeast_KillingsReady: At the table right now: {0} of yours against {1} guests. Give your people time to sit down before you give the signal.
LanguageData.RimFeast_AssassinateDisabledNotSeated: the guests are not at the table yet
LanguageData.RimFeast_StartKillingsDesc: Pick the guest who dies first, the head of the house, if you can reach them. Your nearest able fighter walks up and opens their throat, and the moment blood hits the floor every fighter you have is drafted and thrown at the survivors. Steel against steel, no more ceremony. Children and those incapable of violence stay out of it.\n\nPosition your people before you strike.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageSignalGiven: {0} moves on {1}. When the blood hits the floor, everyone attacks.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextInviteSentPlanned: A messenger rides out with gifts and your invitation to {0}. If all goes well, a cortege will arrive within a day or so.\n\nSet a fine table, and whet the knives. They must suspect nothing until the doors close.
LanguageData.RimFeast_InviteRisky: - cold terms, at your own risk
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextPoisonerCaught: {0} of the cortege of {1} was seen slipping something into the food laid out for the feast. The plot is foiled and the cortege flees your hall.\n\nIt was they who broke the guest right: no house will fault you for whatever befalls poisoners on their way out.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextPoisonSymptoms: Your people are doubling over in the middle of the feast, and the guilty hand belongs to {0}: the cortege of {1} salted your table with poison. They flee your hall.\n\nBurn what remains on that table. And let none weep for what befalls poisoners.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextPoisonRevealed: In the days after the feast, your colonists fall sick one after another, and the truth surfaces: the cortege of {0} poisoned your table and smiled while you toasted their health.\n\nBurn whatever remains of that feast.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextProposal:
{0} of {1} has been struck by your colonist {2} across the feast table, and asks for their hand in marriage.

Accept and {2} weds into the house and rides home with the cortege, sealing a bond of kin between you. You will not see them again, but the house will call you family.

Decline and no harm is done: such things are asked at every great feast.
LanguageData.RimFeast_ProposalAccept: Give your blessing (they wed into the house and leave with the cortege)
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextBetrothed: {0} and {1} are married. As the feast ends, {0} gathers their things and rides out with the cortege of {2}, a noble of the house now. Your halls are quieter, but you have kin among the nobility.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageProposalDeclined: You decline the match. The suitor of {0} takes it in good grace.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextPactOffered: {0} left your hall well fed and well pleased. Their steward will send one of the house merchants your way within a few days, whichever of them can be spared.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextPactChoice: A banquet like that is not soon forgotten. Before riding out, the lord of {0} offers you the pick of the house merchants: name the trade you want and that caravan will be sent within a few days.\n\nSay nothing and their steward will simply send whoever can be spared.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessagePactLapsed: The caravan promised by {0} could not reach your colony, and the agreement lapses.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextJaded: {0} has dined at your table {1} time(s) already. Your hall holds fewer wonders for them now, and their thanks are measured accordingly. Give them a season to forget before you send for them again.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextBrawlDeath: The drunken brawl went too far and a guest of {0} lies dead on your floor, killed by one of their own. The house holds you blameless, but the cortege gathers its cloaks in silence. A corpse under the table ends any banquet.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextGuestsHarmed: A guest of {0} has come to harm under your roof. The cortege storms out, and the house will remember this insult to hospitality.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextGuestsLeaveFighting: Blades came out on your land while the cortege of {0} was under your roof, and one of theirs went down in the fighting. They gather their wounded and pull out. No house holds a raid against its host, but the evening is over.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextGuestsLeaveFightingJudged: They had sat at your table long enough to judge it.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageGuestsLeftNoFeast: The cortege of {0} never reached your hall and has turned back.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageGuestsLeaveWeather: The guests of {0} cannot endure this weather and take their leave.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageInviteVoid: Your invitation to {0} is void: there is no longer a house to receive, or no longer peace between you.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageSpotDestroyed: The feast spot is gone. The invitation to {0} is wasted.
LanguageData.RimFeast_ShowMarkerDesc: Draw the feast spot on the floor. Turn it off and the marker vanishes from your hall while the spot keeps working. You can still click it to select it.
LanguageData.RimFeast_AreaDesc: How far the feast reaches from the spot. Only food, drink, chairs and instruments inside it count, and the guests stay inside it. Select the spot to see it on the floor.
LanguageData.RimFeast_AreaAutoDesc: Stretch the feast to the walls of the room the spot stands in, however big it is.
LanguageData.RimFeast_AreaNotEnclosed: The spot isnt in an enclosed room. Use the radius instead.
LanguageData.RimFeast_AreaFitted: The feast now fills the hall: {0} cells.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SpotAreaRoom: Feast area: the whole hall, {0} cells.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SpotAreaRadius: Feast area: {0} cells around the spot, within this room.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextRequestWeapon: {0} of {1} rises at the head of the table, cup in hand, and speaks at length of the steel your smiths turn out. Then he comes to the point: he would carry one of your blades home. Your {2}.\n\nThe hall has gone quiet. His knights are watching.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextRequestArt: {0} of {1} rises at the head of the table and looks a long moment at {2}, which he has been staring at since the second course. Then he asks whether it might travel home with him.\n\nThe hall has gone quiet. His knights are watching.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextRequestRival: {0} of {1} rises at the head of the table and speaks of {2}, and of what he thinks of them. Then he asks you to swear off that house here and now, in front of everyone.\n\nThe hall has gone quiet. Whatever you answer, it will travel.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextRequestWard: {0} of {1} rises at the head of the table and speaks of his own household, of the boys and girls being raised there, of arms and letters and courtesy. Then he asks for {2}, to serve as a page in his hall and come home when they are old enough to bear arms. Some {3} years.\n\nThey would be under his roof, as he is under yours tonight.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageRequestWardDone: {0} rides out with {1}, to return in some {2} years.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextWardReturns: {0} is back, {2} years old now, riding in from {1}. They left a child and they come back with a sword hand, a courtier's tongue, and letters.\n\nThey have rejoined your colony.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextWardHouseFell: {0} walks through your gate years early, {2} years old. House {1} has fallen, its halls stand empty, and there was nowhere else to go. Whatever they learned there, they bring home.\n\nThey have rejoined your colony.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextWardLost: {0} was being raised in the halls of {1}. Whatever passed between you and that house, no one is riding home. You will not see them again.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextWardDied: Word comes from {1}. {0} died in their household. They send what little there is to send.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextRequestBed: {0} of {1} has been drinking, and has not taken his eyes off {2} for the better part of an hour. Now he rises and asks, more or less politely, whether she might keep him company tonight.\n\nYou can let him put the question to her himself, or answer for her. She may not say what he wants to hear, and he will take that badly.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextRequestBedTaken: {0} of {1} has been drinking, and has not taken his eyes off {2} for the better part of an hour. He knows perfectly well she is {3}'s. He rises and asks anyway, loud enough for the whole table.\n\nYou can let him put the question to her himself, or answer for her. She may not say what he wants to hear, and he will take that badly.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageBedAccepted: {0} takes {1} by the hand and leaves the hall. The house is delighted.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageBedRefused: {0} turns him down flat, in front of the whole table. {1} does not take it well.
LanguageData.RimFeast_RequestSteel: He can have my answer in steel
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageAnsweredInSteel: {0} asked, standing. He will not sit back down.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageRequestWeaponDone: The {0} is carried to the head of the table. {1} is pleased.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageRequestArtDone: {0} is taken down from your hall and loaded onto their wagon. {1} is pleased.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageRequestRivalDone: You swear off {0} before the whole hall. {1} is pleased.
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageRequestRefused: You refuse {0} in front of their knights.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetRequestsTip: Halfway through the feast, the head of the cortege may rise and ask a favour of you: a blade from your forge, a piece of art from your hall, a child to raise as a page in his own household, a night with one of your people if he has drunk enough to ask, or that you swear off a rival house. Granting it costs and pays. Refusing insults them.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetRequestChance: Chance of a request: {0}% per feast
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextAwayInvited: A rider comes from {0}. They are setting their own table at {1}, and they would have you at it.\n\nIt is roughly {2} days of travel. Send a caravan to their gates, and send someone who can hold a conversation, it will matter more than what you carry. The invitation stands for {3} days.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetAwayRisk: Risk at their table: {0}% of normal
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetAwayMaxTravel: Houses more than {0} days of travel away do not invite you
LanguageData.RimFeast_AwaySeatInspect: A feast is being held here for you ({0} days left).
LanguageData.RimFeast_MessageAwayNoDiplomat: Nobody in this caravan is fit to sit at a noble table.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextAwayKnives: The feast at {0} went the way feasts go. Good meat, better drink, and their lord on his feet with a cup raised to your health.\n\nThen the doors closed and the men along the wall drew steel. Whatever your people did next, they did with a full stomach and no armour on.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextAwayKnivesHurt: {0} was carried out of it and back to the caravan, in a bad way.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextAwayKnivesClean: Every one of them cut their way to the door and rode out. Nobody will believe it either.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextAwayAmbush: Your people never reached the gates. {0} took them a mile short of the walls, where there would be no witnesses and no table to break the guest right at.\n\nThey are on their own out there.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextAwaySlight: {0} sat your people at the far end of the hall, served them last, and sent them home before the music started. Everyone in that hall understood exactly what was meant.
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextAwayDull: Your people ate at the table of {0}, said the right things, and rode home. Nothing was gained and nothing was lost, which is more than some evenings manage.
LanguageData.RimFeast_LabelAwayFine: A good evening at their table
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextAwayFine: {0} kept a fine hall and your people did you credit in it. Goodwill improved by {1}.
LanguageData.RimFeast_LabelAwaySongs: They will be talking about it
LanguageData.RimFeast_TextAwaySongs: Your people were the talk of the hall of {0}. Their lord would not let the caravan leave empty. Goodwill improved by {1}.\n\nThey ride home with {2}.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetAwayFeastsTip: A house that has dined at your table, or thinks well enough of you already, will eventually set its own and ask you to come. Send a caravan to the marked tile. How the evening goes depends on your best negotiator, on how well they think of you, on how often they have eaten at your table, and on whether you once butchered their cortege.
LanguageData.RimFeast_SetAwayDays: An invitation arrives about every {0} days
LanguageData.RimFeast_SpotLeaderLine: {0}, head of the house, is here in person. Goodwill from this evening counts half again.
